notes.definition: Viral diseases are communicable diseases caused by viruses, which reproduce inside host cells and damage them. You need to know measles and HIV in humans and tobacco mosaic virus (TMV) in plants.
explanation: Measles is a viral disease. Its symptoms are a fever and a red skin rash. Measles is a serious illness that can be fatal if complications arise, for example if the infection spreads to the lungs or brain. The measles virus is spread by inhalation of droplets from the sneezes and coughs of an infected person, so it passes easily between people who are close together. There is no drug that kills the measles virus, so prevention is very important: most young children are vaccinated against measles.

HIV (human immunodeficiency virus) initially causes a flu-like illness a few weeks after infection. After this the person may feel well for many years, but the virus is still present. Unless it is successfully controlled with antiretroviral drugs, the virus attacks the body's immune cells, which are a type of white blood cell. Antiretroviral drugs do not cure HIV, but they stop the virus reproducing, so the immune system is protected and the person can live a long, healthy life.

Late stage HIV infection is called AIDS (acquired immune deficiency syndrome). AIDS occurs when the body's immune system becomes so badly damaged that it can no longer deal with other infections or cancers. People with AIDS do not usually die from HIV itself but from these other infections. HIV is spread by sexual contact or by the exchange of body fluids such as blood, which happens when drug users share needles. Using condoms and not sharing needles reduce its spread.

Tobacco mosaic virus (TMV) is a widespread plant pathogen. It affects many species of plants, including tomatoes and tobacco. TMV gives a distinctive 'mosaic' pattern of discolouration on the leaves: patches of the leaf become pale or yellow because chlorophyll is destroyed. With less chlorophyll, the leaf absorbs less light, so the rate of photosynthesis falls. The plant then makes less glucose for growth, so infected plants grow less well and crops give a lower yield.

All three diseases show the general features of viruses. The virus enters host cells and reproduces inside them, damaging the cells. Viral diseases are hard to treat because drugs that destroy the virus may also damage the host's cells. This is why preventing spread, by vaccination, avoiding contact with infected body fluids, or removing infected plants, is so important.
keyFacts: Measles symptoms: fever and a red skin rash.
Measles can be fatal if complications arise, so most young children are vaccinated against it.
Measles is spread by inhalation of droplets from sneezes and coughs.
HIV initially causes a flu-like illness.
Unless controlled with antiretroviral drugs, HIV attacks the body's immune cells.
Late stage HIV infection (AIDS) occurs when the immune system is so damaged it cannot deal with other infections or cancers.
HIV is spread by sexual contact or exchange of body fluids such as blood, for example when drug users share needles.
TMV is a widespread plant virus affecting many species, including tomatoes.
TMV causes a mosaic pattern of discolouration on leaves.
TMV reduces growth because the discoloured leaves carry out less photosynthesis.

keyTerms.definition: A viral disease causing fever and a red skin rash, spread by inhaling droplets from coughs and sneezes.
Human immunodeficiency virus: a virus that, unless controlled, attacks the body's immune cells.
Late stage HIV infection, when the immune system is so damaged it can no longer deal with other infections or cancers.
Drugs used to control HIV by stopping the virus reproducing; they do not cure the infection.
A widespread plant virus that causes a mosaic pattern of discolouration on leaves, reducing photosynthesis and growth.
White blood cells that defend the body against pathogens; these are the cells attacked by HIV.

workedExamples.title: Explaining the effect of TMV on a crop
workedExamples.question: Explain why tomato plants infected with tobacco mosaic virus produce fewer tomatoes.
steps: TMV causes a mosaic pattern of discoloured (pale) patches on the leaves.
The discoloured parts have less chlorophyll, so they absorb less light.
Less photosynthesis takes place, so the plant makes less glucose.
Less glucose is available for respiration and to make new substances for growth and fruit.
workedExamples.answer: Discoloured leaves have less chlorophyll, so less photosynthesis happens and less glucose is made for growth, giving fewer tomatoes.

workedExamples.title: Explaining why people with AIDS die of other infections
workedExamples.question: Explain why a person with late stage HIV infection may die from an infection that a healthy person would recover from.
steps: Uncontrolled HIV attacks the body's immune cells (white blood cells).
Over time the number of immune cells falls and the immune system is badly damaged.
The body can no longer destroy other pathogens or cancer cells.
So an otherwise mild infection can become serious or fatal.
workedExamples.answer: HIV has destroyed so many immune cells that the immune system cannot fight the other infection.

workedExamples.title: Percentage change in measles cases
workedExamples.question: After a vaccination programme, measles cases in a country fell from 4800 a year to 120 a year. Calculate the percentage decrease.

misconceptions.wrong: Students often think HIV and AIDS are the same thing.
misconceptions.right: In fact HIV is the virus; AIDS is the late stage of HIV infection, when the immune system is badly damaged.

misconceptions.wrong: Students often think people die directly from HIV.
misconceptions.right: In fact people with AIDS die from other infections or cancers that the damaged immune system can no longer deal with.

misconceptions.wrong: Students often think antiretroviral drugs cure HIV.
misconceptions.right: In fact they control the virus by stopping it reproducing; the person still has HIV.

misconceptions.wrong: Students often think TMV kills plants by poisoning them.
misconceptions.right: In fact TMV discolours leaves so there is less chlorophyll, reducing photosynthesis and therefore growth.

misconceptions.wrong: Students often think measles is a mild childhood illness so vaccination is not needed.
misconceptions.right: In fact measles can be fatal if complications arise, which is why most young children are vaccinated.

realWorld: The MMR vaccine given to young children in the UK protects against measles; outbreaks occur where vaccination rates fall.
Antiretroviral treatment means people with HIV who take their medicine can have a near-normal life expectancy.
Needle exchange schemes give drug users clean needles to reduce the spread of HIV through shared blood.
Tomato growers remove infected plants, disinfect tools and grow TMV-resistant varieties to protect yields.
examTips: For TMV always make the full chain: discolouration, less chlorophyll, less light absorbed, less photosynthesis, less glucose, less growth.
For HIV, say the virus attacks immune cells (white blood cells), not just 'the immune system'. Mention antiretroviral drugs if asked about control.
Learn the two spec symptoms of measles exactly: fever and a red skin rash.
Do not say antibiotics treat viral diseases. Antibiotics only work on bacteria.
summary: Measles: virus, fever and red rash, spread by droplets, can be fatal, so young children are vaccinated.
HIV: flu-like illness at first, then attacks immune cells unless controlled by antiretroviral drugs.
AIDS: late stage HIV when the immune system cannot deal with other infections or cancers.
HIV spreads by sexual contact and exchange of body fluids such as blood from shared needles.
TMV: plant virus causing a mosaic of discoloured leaves, reducing photosynthesis and growth.

questions.question: Which pair of symptoms is caused by measles?
options: Fever and a red skin rash
Thick yellow discharge and pain when urinating
markScheme: 1 mark: fever and a red skin rash
questions.explanation: Measles causes a fever and a red skin rash. Diarrhoea and vomiting are symptoms of Salmonella food poisoning, a discharge and painful urination are symptoms of gonorrhoea, and recurrent fever is typical of malaria.

questions.question: How is the measles virus spread?
options: By inhalation of droplets from sneezes and coughs
markScheme: 1 mark: inhalation of droplets from sneezes and coughs
questions.explanation: Measles is airborne: droplets from an infected person's coughs and sneezes are breathed in. Mosquitoes spread malaria, needles spread HIV and undercooked chicken spreads Salmonella.

questions.question: What type of pathogen causes tobacco mosaic disease in plants?
markScheme: 1 mark: a virus
questions.explanation: TMV stands for tobacco mosaic virus. Rose black spot is caused by a fungus and malaria by a protist.

questions.question: Which cells does HIV attack if it is not controlled with drugs?
markScheme: 1 mark: immune cells (white blood cells)
questions.explanation: HIV attacks the body's immune cells, which are white blood cells. This gradually destroys the immune system.

questions.question: What is AIDS?
options: The virus that causes flu-like illness
Late stage HIV infection, when the immune system can no longer deal with other infections
A bacterial infection spread by sexual contact
markScheme: 1 mark: late stage HIV infection when the immune system can no longer deal with other infections
questions.explanation: AIDS is the late stage of HIV infection. HIV is the virus; antiretroviral drugs control it; gonorrhoea is the bacterial STD in the spec.

questions.question: Which of the following is a way that HIV is spread?
markScheme: 1 mark: drug users sharing needles
questions.explanation: HIV is spread by sexual contact or exchange of body fluids such as blood, which happens when drug users share needles. It is not spread through the air, water or by mosquitoes.

questions.question: Why does TMV reduce the growth of an infected plant?
options: It blocks the xylem so water cannot reach the leaves
It produces toxins that kill the roots
The discoloured leaves carry out less photosynthesis
It makes the stomata close permanently
markScheme: 1 mark: the discoloured leaves carry out less photosynthesis
questions.explanation: TMV causes a mosaic of discoloured patches. These have less chlorophyll, so less photosynthesis happens and less glucose is made for growth.

questions.question: A person with HIV takes antiretroviral drugs every day. Which statement best describes the effect of the drugs?
options: They kill all the virus particles so the person is cured
They stop the virus reproducing, protecting the immune cells
They act as a vaccine, so the person makes antibodies against HIV
They kill the bacteria that cause AIDS
markScheme: 1 mark: they stop the virus reproducing, protecting immune cells
questions.explanation: Antiretroviral drugs control HIV rather than curing it. By stopping the virus reproducing, they prevent it attacking immune cells, so AIDS does not develop. AIDS is not caused by bacteria and the drugs are not a vaccine.

questions.question: Measles spreads very quickly in schools where few children are vaccinated. Which feature of measles best explains this?
options: It is spread by droplets in the air, so close contact is not needed for transmission
It is spread only by sexual contact
It is carried by a vector that lives in schools
It can only infect children who already have HIV
markScheme: 1 mark: it is spread by droplets in the air
questions.explanation: Airborne droplets from coughs and sneezes can be inhaled by anyone nearby, so in a classroom one infected child can pass the virus to many others. The other options are incorrect descriptions of measles.

questions.question: Which plant is commonly affected by tobacco mosaic virus?
markScheme: 1 mark: tomato
questions.explanation: TMV affects many species of plants including tomatoes (and tobacco). Roses are known in the spec for black spot, a fungal disease.

questions.question: After a vaccination programme began, the number of measles cases in a country fell from 4800 per year to 120 per year. Calculate the percentage decrease in cases.
questions.explanation: Percentage decrease = (decrease ÷ original) × 100 = 4680 ÷ 4800 × 100 = 97.5%.

questions.question: In a region, 650 000 young children are due to be vaccinated against measles. 8% of them are not vaccinated. Calculate how many children are not vaccinated.
questions.explanation: 8% means 8 out of every 100, so multiply by 0.08: 650 000 × 0.08 = 52 000 children.

questions.question: Healthy tomato plants in a greenhouse produced a mean of 4.5 kg of tomatoes each. Plants infected with TMV produced a mean of 3.15 kg each. Calculate the percentage reduction in yield caused by TMV.
questions.explanation: Reduction = 1.35 kg. Divide by the original (healthy) yield: 1.35 ÷ 4.5 × 100 = 30%.

questions.question: A healthy leaf has a green area of 36 cm². After infection with TMV, 9 cm² of the leaf is discoloured and cannot photosynthesise. Assuming the rate of photosynthesis is proportional to green area, calculate the percentage decrease in the leaf's rate of photosynthesis.
questions.explanation: The green area that still photosynthesises is 36 − 9 = 27 cm², so the rate falls by (36 − 27) ÷ 36 × 100 = 25%.

questions.question: Give two symptoms of measles.
markScheme: 1 mark: fever (high temperature)
1 mark: red skin rash
questions.explanation: The specification lists fever and a red skin rash as the symptoms of measles.

questions.question: State why most young children in the UK are vaccinated against measles.
markScheme: 1 mark: measles is serious and can be fatal if complications arise
questions.explanation: Measles is not a trivial illness; complications can kill, so children are vaccinated to prevent it.

questions.question: Give two ways in which HIV can be spread from one person to another.
markScheme: 1 mark: sexual contact
1 mark: exchange of body fluids such as blood, e.g. drug users sharing needles
questions.explanation: HIV is spread by sexual contact and by the exchange of body fluids such as blood, for example when drug users share needles.

questions.question: Describe the symptoms of tobacco mosaic virus and how it affects the plant.
markScheme: 1 mark: mosaic pattern of discolouration on the leaves
1 mark: affects growth because there is less photosynthesis
questions.explanation: TMV shows as a mosaic of discoloured patches on leaves. These parts photosynthesise less, so growth is reduced.

questions.question: Explain how antiretroviral drugs help a person infected with HIV.
markScheme: 1 mark: they control the virus (stop it reproducing)
1 mark: so it does not attack/destroy the immune cells (and AIDS does not develop)
questions.explanation: The drugs keep HIV under control, which protects the immune cells and so prevents the person developing late stage HIV (AIDS).

questions.question: Suggest two ways the spread of HIV could be reduced.
markScheme: 1 mark each for any two: using condoms; not sharing needles (needle exchange schemes); treating infected people with antiretroviral drugs; screening donated blood
questions.explanation: Each method stops body fluids being exchanged between an infected and an uninfected person.

questions.question: Explain why a farmer's tomato crop infected with TMV produces less fruit than an uninfected crop.
markScheme: 1 mark: leaves become discoloured, so they have less chlorophyll
1 mark: so less light is absorbed and less photosynthesis happens
1 mark: so less glucose is made for growth/making fruit
questions.explanation: The marks come from the full chain of reasoning: discolouration, less chlorophyll, less photosynthesis, less glucose for growth and fruit.

questions.question: Explain why people with AIDS often die from infections such as pneumonia, which healthy people usually survive.
markScheme: 1 mark: HIV has attacked/destroyed immune cells (white blood cells)
1 mark: so the immune system is badly damaged
1 mark: so it cannot destroy the pathogens causing other infections
questions.explanation: HIV does not usually kill directly. By destroying immune cells it leaves the body unable to fight other infections or cancers.

questions.question: Measles and HIV are both viral diseases. Suggest why measles spreads through a population much faster than HIV.
acceptedAnswers: HIV needs sexual contact or blood
markScheme: 1 mark: measles is spread through the air by droplets, so anyone nearby can be infected
1 mark: HIV needs exchange of body fluids (sexual contact or blood), which happens much less often
questions.explanation: Breathing in droplets is an everyday event, whereas HIV transmission requires specific contact with body fluids.

questions.question: Describe the symptoms, spread and control of measles.
markScheme: Indicative content: viral disease; symptoms: fever and red skin rash; can be fatal if complications arise; spread by inhalation of droplets from sneezes and coughs; controlled by vaccination of young children; isolating infected people; covering coughs and sneezes.
Level 2 (3 to 4 marks): accurate description covering symptoms, spread and control.
Level 1 (1 to 2 marks): some correct points from one or two areas.
0 marks: no relevant content.
questions.explanation: A complete answer covers all three parts of the question: symptoms (fever, rash), spread (droplets) and control (mainly vaccination).

questions.question: Describe how HIV infection develops if it is not treated, and explain how the spread of HIV and its effects can be controlled.
markScheme: Indicative content: HIV is a virus spread by sexual contact or exchange of body fluids such as blood (shared needles); first causes a flu-like illness; virus reproduces inside cells; it attacks the body's immune cells (white blood cells); immune system becomes badly damaged; late stage HIV infection (AIDS); body can no longer deal with other infections or cancers. Control: antiretroviral drugs stop the virus reproducing so immune cells are protected and AIDS does not develop; condoms prevent exchange of body fluids during sex; not sharing needles / needle exchange; testing and screening blood.
Level 3 (5 to 6 marks): detailed, logically ordered description of the course of infection AND clear explanation of several control methods linked to how they work.
Level 2 (3 to 4 marks): description of the course of infection with some control methods, or detailed treatment of one part.
Level 1 (1 to 2 marks): simple, unlinked statements.
0 marks: no relevant content.
questions.explanation: Higher-level answers describe the stages in order (flu-like illness, attack on immune cells, AIDS, other infections) and explain how each control method reduces spread or protects the immune system.

questions.question:
A gardener grows tomatoes. Some plants develop leaves with a pale mosaic pattern.
Explain the cause of these symptoms and how the disease affects the tomato plants.
markScheme: Indicative content: caused by tobacco mosaic virus (TMV); a plant pathogen affecting many species; causes discolouration of leaves in a mosaic pattern; discoloured areas lack chlorophyll; less light absorbed; less photosynthesis; less glucose produced; slower growth and lower yield of tomatoes.
Level 2 (3 to 4 marks): names TMV and gives a linked explanation of how it reduces growth.
Level 1 (1 to 2 marks): identifies the virus or gives an effect without linking it to photosynthesis.
0 marks: no relevant content.
questions.explanation: Name the pathogen (TMV, a virus) and explain the chain from discolouration to reduced photosynthesis and growth.

questions.question: What is the first illness a person usually has after becoming infected with HIV?
markScheme: 1 mark: a flu-like illness
questions.explanation: HIV initially causes a flu-like illness. A red rash is a symptom of measles, painful urination of gonorrhoea, and food poisoning of Salmonella.
